title: 10-year-old with leg stiffness after long walks and a history of early absence seizures

provenance.citation: Synthetic case drafted 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: Parents: "After long walks or sports, especially before lunch, her legs twist and she has to sit down for half an hour."
history_of_present_illness: Since age 7, episodes of dystonic stiffening and twisting of both legs, sometimes with choreic movements, lasting 10–40 minutes, occurring after 15+ minutes of continuous exercise. More likely when she has skipped breakfast or before meals; parents noticed a sugary snack seems to help her recover. Absence seizures began at age 2.5, partially responsive to valproate; currently on levetiracetam with occasional breakthrough absences. Mild learning difficulties in mathematics and reading. Occasional unsteadiness in the morning before breakfast.

symptom_timeline.event: Valproate, partial response; switched later to levetiracetam
Episodes increase with school sports; referral

movement_findings.observation: Parent video (physician-reviewed): after a 25-minute walk, bilateral foot inversion and dystonic leg posturing with intermittent chorea, lasting ~20 minutes, improving with rest.
Interictal: mild gait ataxia on tandem; no dystonia at rest.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Mild difficulties with attention and arithmetic
neurological_exam.other: Head circumference 25th percentile; examined at 11 AM, had breakfast

neurophysiology.report: Generalized 3–4 Hz spike-wave discharges, more frequent in fasting state per note.

prior_workup_and_opinions: Previous view: early-onset absence epilepsy plus unrelated exercise-induced cramps.
